# Data file formats

## There are many different file formats for data... {.smaller}

-   \*.csv
-   \*.tsv
-   \*.txt
-   \*.xlsx (Excel)
-   \*.sav (SPSS)
-   \*.mat (MATLAB)
-   \*.RData (R)
-   \*.EDF (EEG data)
-   \*.xml
-   \*.json
-   \*.yml / \*.yaml
-   ... and many, many more

## and sometimes one can find data in weird places...

-   \*.docx
-   \*.pdf
-   \*.jpeg (images)
-   ... and many more

## Where can you find data? {.smaller}

-   <https://osf.io/>
-   <https://figshare.com/>
-   <https://openneuro.org/> (brain imaging)

-   <https://openpsychologydata.metajnl.com/>
-   <https://openpsychometrics.org/\_rawdata/>
-   <https://dataverse.harvard.edu/>
-   <https://nimh-dsst.github.io/OpenCogData/>

https://guides.library.cmu.edu/artificial-intelligence/datasets https://guides.library.ucla.edu/psychology/data https://datatools.samhsa.gov/ https://github.com/awesomedata/awesome-public-datasets https://github.com/awesomedata/awesome-public-datasets?tab=readme-ov-file#neuroscience https://datahypothesis.com/free-public-datasets-data-analyst-must-know/

## Which file format should you choose?

-   use open file formats
-   use a format that fits your use case

# Importing data into R

## Importing data into R

-   R can import a large range of data formats,
-   but you typically need a particular package for a particular file format: `readr` (CSV, TSV), `readxl` (Excel), `haven` (SPSS, Stata, SAS)
-   all three are installed with the tidyverse, but `library(tidyverse)` loads only `readr`: load the others with `library(readxl)` and `library(haven)`
-   RStudio also offers a point-and-click import: *File → Import Dataset*

## Where does R look for files?

-   R reads and writes files relative to its **working directory**; see it with `getwd()`
-   open the lab's project file (`lab_import_data.Rproj`): RStudio sets the working directory to the lab folder
-   code chunks in a `.qmd` file run in the folder of that file: for the lab files, that is the lab folder too
-   so `"datasets/booksales.csv"` means "the file `booksales.csv` in the `datasets` folder of the lab"

## Relative vs absolute paths

-   relative: `read_csv("datasets/booksales.csv")` works on any computer that has the lab folder
-   absolute: `read_csv("C:/Users/anna/Downloads/R-intro-labs/lab_import_data/datasets/booksales.csv")` works only on Anna's computer
-   tip: inside the quotes, press **Tab** and RStudio completes file and folder names for you

# Data frames (aka spreadsheets)

## Data frames

-   Data frames are likely the most important data structure in R.
-   They are basically like a spreadsheet.
-   `read_csv()` returns a *tibble*: the tidyverse's version of a data frame (you will see "A tibble: 14,999 × 10")
-   There are a few fundamental operations that you must know how to perform on data frames.

## Main operations on data frames

0.  Inspect the size and type of a data frame
1.  See the content of a data frame
2.  Select a column of a data frame
3.  Filter rows of a data frame
4.  Modify or create new columns (mutate)
5.  Save a data frame (e.g., as a csv file)

## Example dataset

The `data_frames.qmd` exercises use the `Employee satisfaction and Salary (ESS)` dataset, downloaded from [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/13935313).
